review.verdict: The blueprint style and typo gag are charming, but the robots' arms cross right over the misspelled word and highlight, cluttering the exact spot the joke depends on and undercutting the pinky-swear read — this needs a layout fix before it's publish-ready.
revisionNotes: The inner arms/hands of robot-left and robot-right cross directly over the 'ZTATES' label and its highlight ellipse — that's the punchline and must not be occluded. Route the pinky-link lower, over a small desk component (per brief), so hands meet below the document instead of across its face.
Add the 'desk' prop called out in the brief ('link pinky fingers over a desk') — right now the gesture reads as crossed/broken arms, not a recognizable pinky-swear, weakening the central metaphor.
Scale robots to ~0.9 and/or increase the x offset on left-third/right-third anchors so their heads stop clipping the document's side border.

Recolor highlight-ztates: the r-glow ellipse renders as a muddy olive-brown against the blue grid and pale text, lowering contrast on the one word that must pop. Use a brighter, more saturated yellow fill.

Increase vertical spacing between the 'PLEDGE' header/underline and the 'UNITED'/'ZTATES' lines so the signature circle and the robots' arm-crossing zone don't compete for the same band of the document.

review.verdict: Passes: the blueprint style is clean and the UNITED/ZTATES typo reads instantly, but the supposed pinky-swear — the whole metaphor of a solemn pledge reduced to a kid's gesture — doesn't actually land because the two inner hands just sit apart on the desk instead of linking.
revisionNotes: The pinky-swear is the core metaphor but doesn't read: the two inner hand-circles sit on the desk with a gap instead of interlocking. Angle the robots' inner arms so the yellow hand-circles overlap/hook together, closing the gap so it clearly reads as linked pinkies.

The outward-pointing arms (stretched to the canvas edges) don't serve the joke and add visual noise/competing focal points; consider dropping them or swapping to a pose where both arms converge on the desk.
Lower third of the frame is empty once the robots' legs end; nudge the robot/desk group up slightly or add a thin ground line/shadow to anchor them and better fill the square.
Keep the PLEDGE/UNITED/ZTATES typo treatment as-is — it's legible, bold, and the yellow highlight on ZTATES reads instantly as the joke's punchline.
